newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann sees early breakeven at AOL Europe.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann sees early breakeven at AOL Europe.

text.p: German publishing group Bertelsmann AG said on Monday its European joint venture with the computer network America Online would be profitable two years ahead of schedule.
"AOL in Europe will reach breakeven in 1997/98, well ahead of the business plan," Bertelsmann board member Thomas Middelhoff told a news conference in Hamburg.
Middelhoff said AOL currently has around 200,000 subscribers in Europe and that it expected to be the market leader.
Talks over an alliance between Bertelsmann, America Online, Axel Springer Verlag and Deutsche Telekom were close to conclusion, he said.
AOL Europe is expected to take a 33 percent stake in Telekom's online service T-Online and Axel Springer a 5 percent stake.
In exchange, Telekom will take over 20 percent of AOL Europa and roughly a third of the shares in AOL Deutschland Bertelsmann Online.
The two German-language online services T-Online and AOL, which up until now have competed against each other, plan to retain independent brand names.

Telekom confirmed it planned to spin off T-Online into an independent company ahead of the equity swap. The new company will be called Online Pro Dienste GmbH and will be responsible for business planning and marketing of T-Online services.
It will be based in Darmstadt.
After the failure of Europe Online, Luxembourg-based online service that collapsed last week, AOL's only other pan-European competitors are Microsoft Corp's Microsoft Network and CompuServe.

CompuServe has around 700,000 subscribers in Europe. But the company has been losing ground to AOL worldwide and made a loss in its first fiscal quarter, and Middelhoff said he expected only two major global services would survive.
"I believe that eventually two global online services will survive. The first one will be AOL and in my opinion the second one will be Microsoft Network," he said.

Commenting on Bertelsmann's multimedia business, Middelhoff said the company's growing activities in this area would have sales of 350 million marks in the current business year, which ends on June 30.
"That's compared to nil in 1995," he said.
Middelhoff said he was confident Bertelsmann would reach its target of two billion marks in turnover in multimedia by the year 2000.
"We are convinced that we will be the market leader in Europe," he added.
